description: Sinusoidal load disturbance at 0.05 Hz to demonstrate RepetitiveController advantage over PID/MPC. Plant starts at Medium Load (op B). A sinusoidal perturbation on y1 setpoint simulates periodic grid load oscillations at 0.05 Hz (period = 200 s). After one learning period, RepetitiveController should achieve near-zero periodic IAE; PID and MPC retain residual periodic error proportional to their disturbance-rejection bandwidth.

_notes.periodic_amp: Sinusoidal setpoint amplitude [bar, MW, -] imposed on top of the operating-point output. y1: ±5 bar pressure swing; y2: ±2 MW power demand swing; y3: uncontrolled (ESC-only).
_notes.periodic_freq_hz: 0.005 Hz = period of 200 s. RepetitiveController periodSteps = 200. After one period (200 s), the repetitive buffer learns the full disturbance waveform and cancels it feed-forward. A faster frequency (e.g. 0.05 Hz, period 20 s) can also be used but requires periodSteps=20 and amplitudes scaled down.
_notes.duration_s: 7200 s = 36 repetitive periods. Gives PID, MPC, and RepetitiveController time to show long-term periodic-error behaviour clearly in the CSV logs.

validation_criteria.RepetitiveCtrl_steady_periodic_IAE_fract: After t >= 400 s (2 learning periods), the running IAE rate for RepetitiveCtrl should be < 5% of the PID running IAE rate. Computed as: d(IAE_y1)/dt integrated over [400,7200] / d(IAE_y1)/dt for PID over the same window.
validation_criteria.PID_periodic_error_visible: PID y1 error trace should show persistent sinusoidal residual at 0.005 Hz with amplitude >= 1 bar throughout the run.
validation_criteria.MPC_periodic_error_visible: MPC y1 error trace should show residual periodic error at 0.005 Hz, smaller than PID but larger than RepetitiveCtrl after the learning period.
validation_criteria.all_controllers_stable: No NaN, no divergence, valve positions must remain in [0, 1] at all times.
